citations.review_text:
[h1] There really is NOTHING quite like Firewatch. [/h1]
[h2] No actual spoilers, don't worry! You find all of this out in the first few minutes of the game. [/h2]

I previously had a copy of the game installed on another platform, but, having lost access to it, I decided to buy and play Firewatch on Steam, for the first time in my life (yes, I know I'm ten years "late", but you can never be late for games like this).
I won't bore you with the nitty-gritty details I cover with every game, but I will list them in brief anyway:

- First, expect a fair bit of jank. Firewatch has turned 10 this year, so you better believe there will be some funky collision, your player character glitching around the terrain, audio inconsistensies or the occasional scripted cutscene glitch, and you BETTER show some respect. 
- The graphics aren't much to write home about (hell, I would rather say that the "Ultra" preset is comparable to the modern-day "Medium" or even "Low" at times), but the overall design suits the game extremely well and adds to the atmosphere at every turn.
- I actually enjoyed the game without the soundtrack (or with minimal music) even more than with any track playing in the background, as the realism in walking through a forest with nothing but its' ambience filling your ears is something that immerses you even deeper into the game. 

But, as you will quickly come to realize, Firewatch is not defined by any of these elements, nor is it any tag you might have seen on the page. Sure, it does horror better than any other game I have seen [spoiler]by not including any actual horror[/spoiler], and it features a wonderful open world [spoiler]that limits your movement regardless[/spoiler], and it has elements of comedy [spoiler]which... you know what, I don't want to spoil anything else. Play the damn game.[/spoiler]
But all of that is not what defines Firewatch. You're playing a walking simulator, whose defining features, at least as to my mind, are the Atmosphere and t…

A kind of short, but really great narrative game, which tells you about people. I really regret buying it on sale, developers should have more of my money honestly.

also you'll encounter some bugs during the play, but they are not that critical.

Honestly, I don't really understand why Firewatch is so loved. I wouldn't call it a bad game, but I just couldn't connect with it.

For me, it felt like a walking simulator with a little bit of a story that never really goes anywhere. The mystery starts off quite interesting, but the more you play, the more you realize that things aren't going to be properly explained. And the open ending didn't really help.

I also couldn't get attached to the characters. Henry and Delilah have some nice conversations, but their relationship never really develops into anything special. The father-and-son storyline also had potential, but it's barely explored beyond a few conversations, photos and notes. I was expecting something much more emotional.

The atmosphere didn't really do it for me either. The soundtrack is barely there, and unfortunately, I can't say I found anything particularly memorable.

And to make things worse, I kept running into bugs that completely broke my movement controls. Interacting with ropes, climbing or descending sometimes made me unable to move at all, forcing me to reload. And this happened way too often.

I really wanted to enjoy Firewatch, but I just don't see what makes it so special. Maybe it's simply not my kind of game, but I finished it feeling more disappointed than anything else.

Great story that hooks you from the very beginning, even though the ending feels a little underwhelming.

The graphics and voice acting are so good that you'll barely notice some of the game's minor flaws.

For example, navigation can be a bit frustrating, as you'll find yourself opening the map every few seconds. There are also a few bugged areas where you can get stuck (bushes, rocks, etc.). I actually had to reload my save twice just to get unstucked.

Overall, definitely a game worth playing through to the end!

100% Steam achievements can be completed fairly easily in around 5–10 hours. There are a few missable achievements, but once you know what to do and where to go, they're pretty easy to get.

claims.claim: Reviewers praise the voice acting performances, specifically highlighting the work of the actors voicing Henry and Delilah.

citations.review_text:
You don't play Firewatch for complex mechanics or action—you play it for the human connection. Set in the Wyoming wilderness in 1989, the game puts you in the boots of Henry, a man taking a summer job as a fire lookout to escape a complicated life back home.
​What makes it special:
​Incredible Voice Acting: Rich Sommer (Henry) and Cissy Jones (Delilah) deliver some of the best performances in gaming. Every walkie-talkie conversation feels natural, witty, and emotionally real.
​Stunning Visuals: The warm, stylized art direction makes every sunset, canyon, and lookout tower feel like a postcard you want to live in.
​Grounded Mystery: Without spoiling anything, the tension builds slowly and realistically, keeping you hooked until the very end.
​Verdict: If you love narrative-driven games, great writing, and atmospheric exploration, don't miss this. Easily a 5/5.

A wonderful narrative experience, with a compelling story that doesn't overstay its welcome, gorgeous art direction, and above all else masterful voice acting, especially Cissy Jones' performance of Delilah. 

Not much in terms of gameplay, but well if you don't like Walking Simulators then don't buy games tagged with it. 

Highly recommended.

[h1] Text Review: [/h1]
Firewatch is a renowned first-person walking simulator full of mystery and eerie moments.
I'm going to start by mentioning the positive aspects.
The voice acting is very good. The way both Henry and Delilah speak made me understand their own feelings.
The sound effects are very good as well. The nature sounds are both relaxing and creepy depending on the location and story progression.
The story is short but it's good. In the end it was a little bit disappointing though.
The visual art is good. It's both cozy and sinister. It's like what I mentioned before, it depends on the circumstance.
The graphics are very good. Both the sunlight and its shadows are really well made.
The only negative aspect I could see is the gameplay. The character movement is kind of slow. Additionally, the path is sometimes blocked by annoying invisible barriers that make no sense being there. One thing is to put invisible barriers on some edges of the map, another is to do it between two trees when going to the lake for the first time.
This paragraph is for the achievement hunters. It's easy to obtain 100% of the Steam achievements. Additionally, there are no tasks that require grinding.


[h1] Recommendation: [/h1]
Firewatch is the first mystery walking simulator I played, and it didn't disappoint me at all. I'm looking forward to playing another game of the sort in the future!
I totally recommend it!

Wish it was a little longer, but overall pretty good experience.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that movement and progression can feel restricted by linear paths and invisible walls blocking off areas.

citations.review_text:
Firewatch is a story-driven game, where you'll explore a Nature Reserve looking to uncover the areas secrets. There's a lot of walking, and talking. It's almost like watching a movie but you walk between scenes.

I would give this game a 6/10. The story was well done, as was the voice acting. The scenery was nice to look at, but I got lost quite a bit as visibility gets lower as the game goes on. There's an open world but not really as it just has a bunch of linear paths you can barely deviate from. There's nothing to really do yourself other than walk from location to location and explore them. 

Achievements, all single player. There's 10 achievements, 5 of which are missable in the main playthrough but you can go back in free roam to pick them up. Takes 5-6 hours for 100%.
